questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence is given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives choose the one which best expresses the sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.

Mr. Puri said to me, "Why are you taking down this fence?"

options.text: Mr. Puri asked me why was I taking down this fence.
Mr. Puri asked me why I was taking down that fence.
Mr. Puri said to me that why are you taking down this fence.
Mr. Puri said to me why you were taking down that fence.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. Mr. Puri asked me why I was taking down that fence.**

**While changing direct speech into indirect speech, interrogative sentences should be changed to assertive sentences.**

 
• Option 1) cannot be the correct answer because **a helping verb has been used before the subject**.
 
• In option 3) **why and that are used simultaneously** which is wrong.
 
• In option 4) **said to is not changed into asked**, so, it cannot be the correct answer.

questions.question:

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

__Lot of peoples__ visit this restaurant as its biryani is famous.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Option 2 - **'Much of people'** is** wrong** because **'much'** is used for the **nouns** that are **uncountable **to specify **quantity **whereas in our case - we are referring to** 'people'**- **Countable noun** for which **'many'** **could** have been the** right** usage.

 
 
• e.g: **Much** of the **sugar** was wasted.
 
• e.g: **Many people** visit this restaurant as its biryani is famous.

 
 
 
 
• Option 3- 'A lot of peoples' doesn't make any sense as
 
 
• the noun** 'people'** does **not** take a **plural from** by adding 's'.
 
• People itself is a collective noun consisting of individuals that form the people.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the most appropriate option is '**A lot of people'**.

Correct sentence: **A lot of people**__ visit this restaurant as its biryani is famous.

(Alternatively: __**Lots of people**__ visit this restaurant as its biryani is famous-could have been the correct usage.)

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The prisoners have made these paintings.

options.text: These paintings were made by the prisoners.
These paintings have been made by the prisoners.
These prisoners have been made by the paintings.
These paintings are made by the prisoners.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 2.**
 
• Option 1 is wrong because the given sentence is in present tense and use of 'were' is wrong.
 
• Option 3 is wrong because in this subject and the object have been interchanged.
 
• Option 4 is wrong because if the active voice is in present perfect tense then the structure followed is 'subject+have+been'.
 
• Therefore Option 2 follows the structure correctly.

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. As he looked at them, their heads began to hang low.

B. Akbar glanced at his courtiers in search of an answer.

C. Once Akbar asked his courtiers a very strange question.

D. The courtiers were dumb-founded by his question.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 3 in which the sentence is arranged in an order**.
 
• The sentence is 'Once Akbar asked his courtiers a very strange question. The courtiers were dumb-founded by his question. Akbar glanced at his courtiers in search of an answer. As he looked at them, their heads began to hang low'.
